We had our pet goat, Fang, many years ago when we lived on a Micronesian island. We got him when he was little and had him tied to a palm tree in the yard so he wouldn't run away. He was so shy he would line himself up behind the tree trunk so you couldn't see him. If you walked around the tree, he would shuffle sideways to keep himself lined up and hidden behind the trunk. After my wife saved him from getting tangled up a couple of times, he realized we were his friends and became a super friendly house/lap goat. When he grew up, he became a little more aggressive and seemingly territorial about things like friends coming to visit. We decided the best thing to do was get him a lady friend and let them run off into the jungle forest together. They were very happy and became the stuff of goat fairy tales. Not the best smelling of pets, but memorable.
Anyone else here have a pet goat? Share stories?

We've had pet goats off and on over the years. I accidentally fed one too many grain calories out of ignorance. As you probably know, goats can tolerate eating a wide variety of substances. Early in my pet goat experience I equated this to goats can eat any amount of anything. I have access to occasional large quantities of out of date pastries. Guess what, goats damn well LOVE out of date pastries. We only had two goats at this time and one day I got a lot of out of date honey buns. When I got home the goats greeted me as usual and I presented them with the whole lot of honey buns right then. They loved it of course, but hours later I discovered the smaller female next to death on the ground. She died almost right after I found her. The bigger male never had a visible problem. This troubled me greatly. We went to the veterinarian and after discussing her symptoms I mentioned the honey buns. That was it. Too many calories too fast. I was devastated that it was my fault. That was a lesson I've never forgotten, just wanted warn others about the dangers of too many honey buns being bad for goats. This was a long time ago so I don't really remember how many there were. Most of the time I would give each goat one or two. This number was several higher than that.
That's sad. And surprising. You may have saved some other pet goat the same fate.

I hope so. I would like to say she died happy. That's not really true at the end, but she was a very happy goat up until her last moments. That's also exactly why I posted the comment, to potentially save some other goat from being fed to death.
She had a great last meal in any event.
As someone who has been there, I feel you.

It sure hurt and was pretty serious, but the number of people in the hospital that came to visit me and ask about goats was hilarious and it was pretty awesome because I got to hear all their goat stories (not that I remember most of them). But yeah, that goat farm was pretty fun. I think another favorite was watching the baby goats jump around all over the place and dance, or try to learn to walk.

What is the largest Aristotelian Substance. (Philosophy was supposed to be fun)--and I know the answer.
How does Aristotle define substance and large? Do you mean in terms of physical size?

Yeah. It needs to be serve a function, be self sufficient and continuous (not multiple separate parts). A chair is a substance, but the wood un-assembled as a working chair is not a substance and is just aggregate mass (the same for a partially constructed chair that does not work [e.g. with two legs]). A mountain is not a substance. Its been a while since I was in school, but it's all in the Metaphysics (which is a major pain), and apparently in the Catagories. In certain terms philosophers trying to define "substance" is pretty crazy over the years, and doesn't really have scientific merit. Descartes says minds true substance, others say only God: in terms of Aristotle it is basically a physical object that serves a function (mass+form=substance). I'm not sure if e.g. the Sun would be a substance in his terms, in general it seems that he refers to man-made things and living things (I could be wrong on that). It's an interesting debate.

I wouldn't say mass and function. Aristotle speaks to substance as the answer to the question "what is it?" and first substance (the actual thing) as that which is neither said of or present in a subject. I think a supernatural being would also meet Aristotle's consideration. Aristotle didn't really consider "mass" in a modern way. He spoke to form and matter in physical things as an answer to change, but that's a very different concept.
